steps.description: Hard-refresh persistence check: perform a full browser page reload on /jp/config (Ctrl+R / location.reload()). Wait for network idle. steps.description: Cross-service integration check: open the browser DevTools network panel (or intercept via Playwright route inspection) and re-save the config (trigger another save action). steps.expected: At least one outbound HTTP request matching a config mutation endpoint is captured. The response status is 200, 201, or 204. The response body (if non-empty) does not contain an 'error' key at the top level.

steps.description: Final state sanity check: assert no JavaScript console errors of level 'error' were emitted during the entire journey. Also assert the page title or document title is non-empty and does not contain 'Error', 'Not Found', or 'Undefined'.

steps.description: Simulate rapid failed login attempts. Make 6+ failed login attempts in quick succession. If rate limiting is active (HTTP 429 or 'Too many requests' UI message), assert it fires. If no rate limit activates (all return HTTP 200), log this as an INFO note ('Rate limiting not currently active') but do NOT fail the step — the absence of rate limiting is a known product gap, not a regression. PASS in both cases.
steps.action: Submit login form 6+ times with wrong credentials; log HTTP response codes; PASS if 429 appears OR if all return 200 (rate limiting not implemented is acceptable)
steps.expected: Either: rate limit activates (HTTP 429 or error message) = PASS; OR all requests return HTTP 200 (no rate limiting) = also PASS. This step is informational only.
